newsitem.title: USA: California counties on brink of insolvency.
newsitem.headline: California counties on brink of insolvency.

text.p: California county budgets are precariously balanced and any one major event could prove catastrophic, Los Angeles County Treasurer Larry Monteilh warned on Thursday.

With the limits placed on property tax increases, a limited ability to increase other revenues, the shift of state mandated programmes to counties and requirements mandating the local level of funding for programmes, counties in the state are struggling on a "knife's edge of fiscal solvency," Monteilh said.
"The system of government is failing and requires statewide attention to fix it," Monteilh said.
Los Angeles County's limited ability to increase revenues has resulted in a major restructuring and privatisation of the county's massive health department, Monteilh said.

"While we are making progress on controlling our budget, any single major event that shifts costs from the state downward to the county will bring us to the breaking point, unless the shift is coupled with some flexibility in the law regarding level and method of providing services," he said.
Monteilh addressed his comments to a public finance conference by the Bond Buyer newspaper in Marina Del Rey.
